subject: Legacy component remediation exception & scan snapshot
messages:
From: Simon Fletcher <security@mercantilebank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@mercantilebank.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request: legacy auth-service scan cadence & remediation commitment

Irene / team,

Mercantile is preparing for an upcoming SIG/SOC2 follow-up and our auditors requested a compact package showing current VM posture for the infra that touches customer auth (auth-service). Specifically we need:

- the last three authenticated scan exports (CSV or export bundle) for auth-service
- current scan cadence (how often auth-service is authenticated + full infra scans)
- remediation SLA for critical CVEs and any exceptions currently active for the auth-service (owner, window, compensating controls)
- planned patch/rollout dates for any pending critical fixes (if known)

We are also tracking a specific CVE that came up in our toolchain: CVE-2026-1745 (affects older nginx module used by auth-service). Please confirm whether Redwood has a remediation plan or compensating control for that CVE and provide any evidence you can (scan ID, ticket, POC).

If possible, please send a short attestation letter we can share with our auditors (one page) confirming cadence and the SLA for critical fixes. Our audit window closes next Friday, so any timing commitments would be helpful.

Thanks,
Simon Fletcher
Head of AppSec – Mercantile Bank
security@mercantilebank.com

--Attachment request: please include last three scan exports (CSV) and any remediation plan PDFs
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Simon Fletcher <security@mercantilebank.com>, Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@mercantilebank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: legacy auth-service scan cadence & remediation commitment

Simon, thanks for the clear list — we can get this over today. High level answers up front:

- Scan cadence: authenticated scans for auth-service run weekly (every Tue 02:00 UTC); full infrastructure scans run monthly (first Sun of month).
- Remediation SLA: standard is 30 days for Critical/High CVEs; exceptions for legacy components are tracked and require documented compensating controls and an agreed risk acceptance window.
- CVE-2026-1745: auth-service is on a legacy nginx module. We have an active mitigation and a staged remediation plan.

Attached: redwood_vm_scan_index.csv (scan IDs + timestamps), cve-2026-1745_remediation_plan.pdf, legacy-auth-compensating-controls.md.

Summary of the CVE plan (short):
- 10/04: deploy additional WAF rule to block exploit paths (mitigation) — executed as emergency config change (owner: Marcus Lin).
- 10/07: canary patch rollout to 5% of auth-service instances in us-west (owner: Marcus Lin).
- 10/11: full rollout scheduled pending canary verification; rollback plan in place.

For the auth-service exception: we are proposing a 60-day remediation window for the legacy nginx module with compensating network-level WAFs and enhanced telemetry (audit logging and IDS rules). If Mercantile can accept this window, we will provide a signed attestation and include the exception in our SOC2 evidence binder. Otherwise, we will accelerate to a 30-day SLA and prioritize the patch — that would require an earlier full rollout and a brief maintenance window.

Let me know which option you prefer and we will attach the attestation.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--Attachments: redwood_vm_scan_index.csv (CSV), cve-2026-1745_remediation_plan.pdf (PDF), legacy-auth-compensating-controls.md (MD)
From: Simon Fletcher <security@mercantilebank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Hayes <sara.hayes@mercantilebank.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence request: legacy auth-service scan cadence & remediation commitment

Irene — thanks for the quick reply and the concrete dates. A few clarifying items: 

1) The auditors will accept a documented exception only if there is a compensating control and a formal attestation that includes owner, agreed window, and confirmation of monitoring. The 60-day proposal is acceptable in principle but we need the attestation letter (one page) signed by your security lead plus a short verification checklist (what you will monitor during the 60-day window).

2) For the CVE specifically: please include the ticket ID (or scan ID) and the initial mitigation timestamp (we need a timestamp and evidence the WAF rule was applied).

3) If you can get the attestation and the monitoring checklist in the next 24 hours, that should satisfy our auditor.

We will plan to accept the 60-day exception provided the attestation and monitoring checklist are present. Please send the attestation as a PDF and, if possible, a DocuSign link so our procurement can keep the record.

Thanks again — appreciate the responsiveness.
Simon
